description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale ranging from 60 to 80. The "Base" method, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 61.5% and shows a steady increase to about 66.5% as the co-occurrence number increases. The "MEND" method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, begins at around 65.5% and rises to approximately 74%. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 62.5% and increases to roughly 68.5%. The "MEMIT" method, represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, begins at approximately 66.5% and climbs to about 72.5%. The "ROME" method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 72.5% and increases to approximately 77.5%. All five methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
